
*How Many are At-Risk: Assessing the Coverage of Traffic Volume Counters in Canadian Cities*

**Objectives: To assess the spatial and temporal coverage of killed or seriously injured victims by permanent or temporary counters in Montreal, Toronto, and Calgary**

**Abbreviations: **
KSI = killed or seriously injured

**NOTE**
When I write for example ksi_CITY.. it means CITY is reaplaced with the name of actual cities like tor (Toronto) or the same things for counters for exmaple perm_CITY_unique
CITY could be tor (Toronto) or cal (Calgary)

##### Centerlines ------------------------------------------------------------
Our GIS analyst, used the centerlines of cities available on the city websites, and cleaned them
to remove non-road elements as well as freeways and expressways. Thus, this datasets is not publicly available
as these were created for the broader CapaCITY project. 
For each road segment in these datasets, relevant attributes such as road class and geomert were included. 

##### Collision datasets ------------------------------------------------------------

## Victim-level not collision level
For all cities, victim-level datasets were used. For exmaple, a collision could have more than 1 injured person.
By considering victim-level we take into account all injured individuals rather than one collision.

Note for Montreal: The island of Montreal includes the City of Montreal and 15 independant municpalities. 
Our study only included the City, so as showin the codes both for KSI and counters, these 15 municpalities were found and 
excluded to focus only on the City of Montreal. 


## Join KSIs with centerline
Each KSI was joined to their nearest road segment to have that road segment attributes.

## ksi_CITY_seg_month
For each ksi_CITY, *ksi_CITY_seg_month* was created. For variance calculations, sum of ksi per month and road segment
is required and this dataset will be used in the Step 5 of Expected Coverage calculation.
i.e., numebr of KSIs in each segment in one month (i.e., segment-month). This is important as one segment-month with 5 KSIs 
should be treated differently that one segment-month with 1 KSI.


*If imported datasets were collision-level, we conerted them to victim-level*. 

Date period was based on the start of Vizion Zero plan in each city, meaning that the first full-year was considered as the
first year until the most available date. 

##### Permanent Counters ------------------------------------------------------------
I will explain the general guideline here, and some steps that were specific to each city below.

The points of all the codes in this section was to create *perm_CITY_unique*, which includes unique
permanent counters with a unique ID for each of them, and a column specifying the type of them
(so after combining them with temporary counters, it is clear these are permanent counters). A 10-meter buffer
was created around each counter to specify the covered road segments by each counter. 

For Toronto and Calgary, permanent counters were used in our analysis. Since our approach depended on what we have here,
I will explain what the codes did for these cities in 2 Categories for these 2 Cities.

For Toronto, Miovision counters are used as permanent counters and this data was directly received from the city of toronto, so we 
cannot share them publicly. You may request this data directly by contacting transportation team of the city. 
Miovision counters are located on the intersections of Toronto and after we found the location of 6 of these conters are not exact, 
we manually extracted the coordinates of these counters so we have the ecact location of all of these counters for our analyis.

#### Temporary Counters ------------------------------------------------------------
*temp_CITY_unique* was created for each city to have unique temporay counter with a 10-meter buffer to determine the covered road segments by each of these counters.


#### c_P_t and c_R_t --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
These are counts of permanent (c_R_t) and temporary (c_R_t) counters in each month. R stands for rotating (i.e., temporary)

Created datasets in order in these codes:

*counter_merge*: For cities with both permanent and temporary counters, these were merged and this dataset was created.

*months_df*: a list of all months for each city in the study. 

*counter_clean*: a clean version of *counter_merge* where those rows with missing counter_id or start and end months were excluded.

*monthly_new_perm*: For cities with permanent counters, we wanted to created "new_perm_t", which is the number of new permanent counters
in each month, and for those months without a new permanent counter installed, the missing NA was replaced with 0. This dataset was
resulted from joining *counter_clean* AND *months_df*. 

*counter_months*: In the *counter_clean*, we had one row per permanent counter with start and end months, but we want
one row per month of an active counter. Thus, for temporary counters, as the start and end months were the same, the new created
'month' column here shows the same date as those columns but for permanent counters, every row is broken down into all months
that counter has been active.

*monthly_active_counters*: number of active counters in each month.

*monthly_counter_deployment*: created from joining *months_df* AND *monthly_new_perm* AND *monthly_active_counters* to have
both months with and without an active counter.

#### Observed Coverage --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Explanation in the codes are clear to follow to logic. For each type of counter, both average (for Table 1) and yearly (for the line graph)
were calculated. 

#### Expected Coverage --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
In the Step 2, the reason we used log transforamtion of CI is that after running the codes for the first time, we saw some negetive CI
which does not make sense for probabilities. Thus, we used log transformation to avoid this issue.
